text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.

LONDON - Britain's leading share index powered higher as investors stared down a possible interest rate hike and focused on bullish corporate earnings. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,960.6, up 64.9 points, or 1.33 percent.

FRANKFURT - German shares ended bourse dealings with modest gains as a steady overnight close on Wall Street and a firmer dollar took pressure off the domestic market. The DAX-30 index closed at 4,302.68, up 5.74 points or 0.13 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 4,325.86, up 23.36 points or 0.54 percent.

PARIS - French shares trimmed their losses at the close in lacklustre holiday trade after sinking earlier on fears of a German interest rate hike to protect the mark. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 8.31 points or 0.28 percent at 2,984.10.

ZURICH - Swiss shares closed little changed after a roller-coaster day as the blue chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) hit an early high of 5,835,6 points, dipped to a low of 5,723.6 and finally ended mid-range. The Swiss market index closed at 5765.2, down 5.8 points or 0.10 percent.

MILAN - Italian stocks lost early gains and closed above session lows after a nervous session with the market continuing its recent correction, depressed by the dollar's strength and a poor performance in Italian Btps. The All Share Mibtel index closed at 14324, down 114 points or 0.79 percent.
AMSTERDAM - Dutch shares ended barely changed as weaker bonds and interest rate nerves eroded early market gains. The AEX index closed at 979.59, up 0.24 points or 0.02 percent.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed moderately lower, extending their losses for a third straight session, as the market was still weighed down by worries over Japan's economy and lack of consumption power, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 19514.45, down 153.62 points or 0.78 percent.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed sharply higher, lifted by HSBC Holdings' positive results and strong inflows of liquidity, after setting an all-time high, brokers said. The Hang Seng index closed at 16371.52, up 111.93 points, or 0.69 percent.
SYDNEY - A lifeless Australian share market limped to a flat finish after a directionless day. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2707.6, up 1.6 points or 0.06 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended firm, hitting new record closes on good local and offshore demand as confectionery and snacks firm Afbrand soared to a 226 cents close from its 100 cents issue price, dealers said. The All-share index closed at 7492.6, up 47.4 points or 0.64 percent. The All Gold index closed at 954.0, down 15.9 points or 1.64 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 9183.2, up 73.0 points or 0.80 percent.
